summary: Shannon County, MO tower built by the Missouri Department of Conservation in 1957; NHLR-registered 2013 and described as still staffed in high fire danger, but a Forest Lookouts list marks it Removed.

facts.status_note: Disputed: NHLR describes it as still staffed in periods of high fire danger; a Forest Lookouts list marks it Removed. No dated removal confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts list uses the label THOMASVILLE (FEDERAL), but the NHLR register names the Missouri Department of Conservation as administrator. The story follows the register.
Not resolved. NHLR describes the tower as still staffed in high fire danger periods; the Forest Lookouts list marks it Removed with no date. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Unverified leads, not used in the story: a Missouri Conservation History Facebook post (https://www.facebook.com/MCC1010/posts/thomasville-fire-lookout-tower-this-tower-and-the-surrounding-40-acres-was-sold-/770545715109867/) appears in search snippets to say the tower and 40 acres were sold on GovDeals; the post and the GovDeals listing (https://www.govdeals.com/asset/16/11790) returned 403 or only a title, so the sale is unconfirmed. A second post in search snippets describes a 68-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower northeast of Eminence; it may be a different tower. A search snippet gives a 1951 build year, but the fetched NHLR page says 1957; the fetched page is used. Missing from record: removal date and access level; no source gave either. The brief record's other_names 'Thomasville (Federal)' comes from the Forest Lookouts list.
